mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly higher than during the 30-day pre-signal window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.5% suggests expanding credit availability and consumer confidence, which accelerates equity market valuation growth and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no correlation with HOUST changes (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months indicates weakening demand or supply chain disruptions, which typically precede a decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-contraction window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for three consecutive months during a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises by > 2% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain positive despite the inflation signal (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a strong labor market signal that, when sustained for one month, is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as market participants anticipate wage growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no statistically significant improvement over the 30-day pre-signal window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but proxy via PAYEMS) coupled with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggest shifting demand patterns that can produce regime-dependent positive 20-day returns in expansionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: No significant return difference in contraction vs. expansion regimes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer confidence (indirectly inferred from a combination of labor and monetary proxies) characterized by UNRATE > 6% and FEDFUNDS > 5% for 60 days is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate a prolonged economic downturn.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND FEDFUNDS > 5% for 60 consecutive days
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during the 60-day pre-signal window (t-test p > 0.05).
